purpose: Two optional educational NASA excerpts for the existing lunar explorer website. Media does not replace interactive point/date selection or supply a selected-state calculation.
common_display_notice: NASA example, not the site or date selected in this app.
reuse_note: Specific silent NASA-supplied variants are credited and linked. No narrated/music variant or third-party soundtrack was included. No NASA endorsement is implied.
editorial_authorship: Trim ranges, additional 1.5× speed, posters and descriptive WebVTT are editorial choices for this website; not claims about NASA original editing or app scientific validation.

assets.title: Shadows Near the Moon's South Pole

edit.note: Only temporal trim, 1.5x speed, frame-rate reduction and H.264 re-encode. No scientific values, date labels, synthetic terrain or soundtrack added.

poster.reason: First frame of the chosen close-view interval; illuminated terrain and long shadows are already visible.

captions.authorship: Original descriptive English captions for this edited excerpt; not NASA narration captions.

cues.text: Sunlight shifts across the lunar south-pole terrain.
Long shadows move over ridges and crater floors.

assets.descriptive_transcript: In this NASA visualization, shifting sunlight moves shadows across ridges and crater floors.
assets.caption_transcript: Sunlight shifts across the lunar south-pole terrain. Long shadows move over ridges and crater floors. NASA example. Time is compressed.
assets.visual_context: Close view of lunar south-pole terrain. Original NASA Sun-direction icon, distance scale and time-progress icons are retained.

frame_review.method: Frames extracted from NASA original with ffmpeg and visually inspected using view_image; encoded playback also visually checked in Chromium screenshot.
frame_review.selected_interval_reason: Visible moving terrain shadows without introductory zoom.

science_boundary: NASA illustrative visualization, not a live camera recording.
Example location/time, not the app-selected site or date.

assets.title: Earth and Sun from the Moon's South Pole

edit.note: Only temporal trim, 1.5x speed, frame-rate reduction and H.264 re-encode. No scientific values, date labels, synthetic terrain or soundtrack added.

poster.reason: First sampled, clearly separated Earth disk after emergence. Source92s and94s hide Earth;96s shows emergence;98s shows it above the ridge. Poster is clip-relative4s, not its hidden-Earth opening.

captions.authorship: Original descriptive English captions for this edited excerpt; not NASA narration captions.

cues.text: From Shackleton's rim, distant terrain hides Earth.
Earth comes into view above the ridge.
Earth changes height in this time-compressed NASA example.

assets.descriptive_transcript: From a fixed virtual viewpoint on Shackleton’s rim, Earth emerges above a distant ridge and changes height in the sky.
assets.caption_transcript: From Shackleton's rim, distant terrain hides Earth. Earth comes into view above the ridge. Earth changes height in this time-compressed NASA example.
assets.visual_context: Fixed virtual ground-level viewpoint on Shackleton's rim, looking toward Earth and distant terrain.

frame_review.method: Frames extracted from NASA original with ffmpeg and visually inspected using view_image; encoded playback also visually checked in Chromium screenshot.
frame_review.selected_interval_reason: Earth starts hidden, emerges above distant terrain, changes apparent height; avoids the eclipse in the earlier 50–80 s interval.
